title: Anticoncentration of random spanning trees in graphs with large minimum degree
summary: A classical result by Otter shows that the complete graph has an exponential number of non-isomorphic spanning trees. This was recently extended by Lee to every almost regular graph of sufficiently large degree. In this paper, we consider graphs of large minimum degree. We show that every connected graph $G$ with $n$ vertices and minimum degree $d$ has at least $n^{Ω(d)}$ non-isomorphic spanning trees. This is tight up to the constant factor in the exponent.
